Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Emerson Hayes  
Member ID: W482887207  
Plan: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of North Carolina Commercial/ACA  
Reference number: POC-D52DAC7115-38519  
Requested service: Hip arthroscopy  
CPT: 29914  
Denial date: August 11, 2026  

Dear Member Rights and Appeals:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914. The denial states that the documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

Please reconsider the request based on the complete clinical information summarized below and the enclosed records.

I have had 18 months of progressive hip pain that has not resolved with rest. My symptoms include sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, inability to run or squat, painful and limited range of motion, and positive provocative testing on the affected side.

The diagnosis is confirmed by the MRI arthrogram performed on July 13, 2026. It shows:

- An anterosuperior labral tear;
- Cam-type femoroacetabular impingement;
- An alpha angle of 68 degrees;
- Preserved joint space; and
- Tonnis grade 0.

I have also completed substantial conservative treatment without adequate improvement:

- Twelve weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, with activity modification;
- Twenty physical therapy visits from March 31, 2026, through June 23, 2026, documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- Eight months of NSAID treatment with inadequate relief; and
- A corticosteroid injection on April 28, 2026, which provided only three weeks of partial relief.

These records establish a confirmed structural abnormality, persistent symptoms, functional impairment, and failure of appropriate nonoperative treatment. They also document the relationship between the cam morphology and the anterosuperior labral tear. The preserved joint space and Tonnis grade 0 support that the hip is not affected by advanced joint-space loss or advanced osteoarthritis.

The requested procedure is being recommended by Lindqvist, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, to address the documented cam-type impingement and associated labral tear. The clinical records support that the anticipated benefit of treating the mechanical abnormality and labral pathology outweighs the risks of continued symptoms and functional limitation, and that the procedure is reasonably expected to improve management and function.

The records also document the absence of relevant contraindicating concerns: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, the BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

The Carelon Joint Surgery guideline identified in connection with this type of review includes general requirements concerning confirmation of the diagnosis, review of examination and diagnostic testing, response to prior treatment, expected benefit compared with potential harm, and submission of documentation that accurately reflects the clinical situation and the ordering provider’s intent. This appeal addresses those requirements through the examination findings, MRI arthrogram, treatment history, physical therapy discharge note, functional limitations, and orthopedic surgical recommendation. I am not quoting a procedure-specific Hip Arthroscopy subsection because that subsection was not included in the denial letter or in the material provided to me.

Please conduct a new medical-necessity review using the enclosed documentation and approve hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914.

If Blue Cross NC or Carelon believes additional information is required, please identify each missing document or clinical fact specifically and provide the exact criteria applied to this request, including the applicable version of the Hip Arthroscopy criteria and the clinical reviewer’s documentation requirements. Please also provide the complete clinical rationale for any continued denial.

Enclosures include the MRI arthrogram report, physical therapy discharge note, treatment history, injection record, examination findings, and the orthopedic surgeon’s clinical documentation.

Sincerely,

Emerson Hayes
